title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A and B are small categories, and (A×B)^ is the category of presheaves on A×B. Grothendieck regards Hom(B°,A), the B-diagrams in A such as simplicial objects when B=Δ, as a full subcategory of (A×B)^ through the Yoneda embedding of A in A^. He fixes two projections, using his convention that the subscript names the factor being forgotten.
- p_{B*} : (A×B)^ → A^ is direct image (limit over B°).
- p_{A*} : (A×B)^ → B^ is direct image along the other projection.
- p_A^* : B^ → (A×B)^ is pull-back, giving the presheaf constant in the A-variable.

First claim. If B has a final object e_B, then p_{B*} = (Γ_B)° sends Hom(B°,A) into A. The reason is that a limit over B° of a functor F: B°→A is just evaluation F(e_B), because e_B is initial in B°. He writes this as Γ''_{e_B}. This gives a commutative square of 'global sections' functors: Hom(B°,A) → A^ via p_{B*} (in fact landing in A), Hom(B°,A) → B^ = Hom(B°,Ens) via (Γ_A)°, and then Γ_A : A^ → Ens and Γ_B : B^ → Ens. Both composites give the total global sections of the presheaf on A×B.

Motivating case. B = Δ, so Hom(Δ°,A) = sA, the simplicial objects of A.

Main question: stability of sA under cotensoring by simplicial sets. For M ∈ B^ he defines X^M := Hom(p_A^*M, X), the internal Hom in the topos (A×B)^.
- X^M lies in Hom(B°,A), possibly under finiteness conditions on M, as soon as A has the limits needed. M is a colimit of representables, so X^M is the corresponding limit of the X_b.
- This holds even though Hom(B°,A) does not contain the p_A^*M themselves.
- The adjunction identities follow from the internal-Hom/product adjunction in (A×B)^: Hom_B(X, Y^M) ≅ p_{A*}Hom(X, Hom(p_A^*M,Y)) ≅ p_{A*}Hom(X×p_A^*M, Y) ≅ Hom_B(X×p_A^*M, Y). Here Hom_B denotes the B^-valued (e.g. simplicial-set-valued) Hom.

Footnote. p_A^*M lies in Hom(B°,A) iff, for every b, the constant presheaf on A with value M(b) is representable. That happens iff each M(b) is a singleton and A has a final object, i.e. iff M is the final presheaf and A has a final object.

Purpose: setting up the simplicial enrichment and cotensors (Quillen's 'simplicial closed model category' structure) for sA and its generalisation to B-diagrams, inside the Closed models notes.
errors: Notational only. 'Il suffit que A soit stable par limites ... pour représenter M comme limite de foncteurs représentables': M is a colimit of representables, and X^M is then the corresponding limit. The intended meaning is clear and correct.

The footnote claim is correct. Suppose a constant presheaf with value S is represented by c. Then precomposition with any f: c→c fixes every element of S. Applied to id this forces End(c) = {id}, so S is a singleton and c is final. Grothendieck states this without proof. Note also that X×p_A^*M is only a presheaf, not an object of Hom(B°,A), unless A has the relevant coproducts (tensoring). He tacitly works in (A×B)^, which is legitimate.

ideas.what: Viewing B-diagrams in A as a subcategory of presheaves on A×B. For B with a final object, the limit over B° is evaluation at e_B and stays inside A.
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda embedding of functor categories; limits over categories with an initial object
ideas.where_published: Similar presheaf-on-product manipulations appear in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs

ideas.what: Cotensor X^M of a simplicial object X by a simplicial set M, defined as an internal Hom in the presheaf topos, together with the adjunction Hom_Δ(X,Y^M) ≅ Hom_Δ(X×M,Y).
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial enrichment / cotensoring of sA (simplicial model category axiom SM0)

ideas.what: Criterion for when the constant presheaves p_A^*M lie in Hom(B°,A): only the terminal M, and only when A has a final object.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine set-up of the simplicial cotensor structure on sA (Quillen 1967), phrased in Grothendieck's presheaf-on-product language with general B in place of Δ. It is correct and elementary, with no new result or unexplored connection.
transcription_corrections: The diagram is a commutative square: Hom(B°,A) → A^ (left, unlabelled; this is p_{B*}) and Hom(B°,A) → B^ = Hom(B°,Ens) labelled (Γ_A)°. Then A^ → (point/Ens) labelled Γ_A and B^ → (point/Ens) labelled Γ_B. The transcription's linear rendering loses this square structure.
In 'B^ = Hom(B°, Ens)' the second argument reads 'Ens', as transcribed.
'ne contient pas nécessairement[?]' more likely reads 'ne contient pas en général'.

'Il suffit que A soit stable par limites du type requis' is followed by an inserted 'limites' (underlined) with an arrow '⇐'. This is an insertion clarifying 'limites', not a separate logical implication.
Footnote: 'Mais ceci signifie que M(b) est réduit à un élément et A a objet final. Donc ssi M objet final de B^, et A admet objet final!!' The reading is plausible as given.
